common_name: Nigricans Alpine Cranesbill (Bronze-Leaved New Zealand Geranium)

planting.note: Plant divisions or small container plants in spring in gritty, sharply drained soil in full sun; this diminutive New Zealand species resents winter wet far more than cold.

directions: Nigricans forms a tight, flattened button of finely cut leaves that darken from bronze to near-black through the season, studded with disproportionately small white flowers from late spring into fall. Native to scree and rocky slopes on New Zealand's South Island, its slow, dense habit suits troughs, scree beds, and tight crevices rather than open borders. Keep it lean and sharply drained; rich, wet soil quickly rots the tight rosettes.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; it roots along trailing stems as it spreads.

directions: Dilys shares the G. endressii x G. traversii parentage of its better-known siblings 'Mavis Simpson' and 'Russell Prichard', carrying bright magenta-pink flowers with a darker eye over trailing, soft grey-green foliage from early summer well into fall. Its sprawling, mat-forming habit makes it useful cascading over low walls or filling gaps along a sunny path edge. Shear congested growth back after the first flush to keep the mat tidy and encourage a fresh round of bloom.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, moisture-retentive, well-drained soil in full sun to light partial shade; stake or let sprawl among nearby perennials once flowering.

directions: This old English cultivar, also sold as 'Splish Splash', bears white to pale lilac petals irregularly flecked and streaked with violet-blue, giving each flower a spattered, hand-painted look quite different from the solid blues of most pratense selections. Because the streaking pattern can vary between seedlings, division from a good clone is the surest way to keep the splashy marking true. Cut the whole clump hard to the ground right after the main early-summer flush to tidy the sprawling foliage and often prompt a lighter rebloom.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fertile, consistently moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade in spring, spacing generously for airflow.

directions: Alpha is a lilac-pink RHS Award of Garden Merit meadow phlox that shares its old Dutch breeding line with the white, red-eyed cultivar 'Omega', producing dense, tapering spires of bloom a couple of weeks ahead of tall garden phlox. Like other P. maculata selections, its narrower, glossier, red-tinted stems and columnar flower spikes shrug off powdery mildew far better than P. paniculata in humid summers. Deadhead spent spikes to tidy the clump and prevent off-type seedlings from popping up nearby.
